correctness_confidence.basis: Lean 4.35.0 verification with zero sorry, zero axiom (beyond propext/Quot.sound), and zero Classical.choice across 18 theorems provides exhaustive machine-checked correctness for the algebraic core.

novelty.basis: Pioneering independent constructive verification of Google Research Cogentic's sub-quasi-polynomial discrete logarithm proof mechanisms, establishing exact zero-float certificate auditing.

reproducibility.basis: Complete open-source release with standalone Lean 4 compilation, deterministic Python auditors, 65 pytest checks, and cryptographic manifest verification.

rigor.basis: Immaculate formalization hygiene and rigorous Python integer-only auditing across 16 canonical witnesses and 61 adversarial test vectors with strict AST whitelisting.

significance.basis: Establishes a rigorous cryptographic benchmark and formal verification standard for sub-quasi-polynomial discrete logarithm algorithms in finite fields.

potential_errors: The formalization explicitly scopes out analytic and arithmetic-geometric pillars (such as Waterhouse/Rück existence, Riemann-Roch, Hasse-Weil, and Artin-Schreier/Kummer indecomposability), which remain dependent on the companion preprint [4].
strengths: Exhaustive Lean 4.35.0 constructive verification with zero sorry and zero Classical.choice across 18 core algebraic and inductive theorems.
Rigorous Python integer-only zero-float certificate auditor (DLP-COGENTIC-CERT-1.0) with strict AST whitelisting and robust multi-mode verification.
Comprehensive test suite covering 16 canonical witnesses across characteristics p in {2,3,5,7} and 61 adversarial red-team test cases with exact error-branch assertions.
Clear, honest scoping delineating universal machine-checked proofs from finite exact witness audits and unverified analytic pillars.
strong_novelty_candidates: Constructive Lean 4 formalization of discrete logarithm algebraic sub-lemmas, Moore determinants, and SL2(Z) unimodular elimination without external libraries.
Exact zero-float multi-mode certificate auditing architecture for finite field discrete logarithm proofs and sparse linearized pencils.
summary: This paper delivers an independent, explicitly scoped, zero-floating-point verification companion for Google Research Cogentic's sub-quasi-polynomial discrete logarithm proof. It combines 18 standalone constructive Lean 4.35.0 theorems (zero sorry, zero Classical.choice) with a pure-integer Python auditor (DLP-COGENTIC-CERT-1.0) verifying 16 canonical exact witnesses across p in {2,3,5,7}, exact Theorem 1.2 onset characterization, and 61/61 live adversarial forgery rejections. The manuscript is rigorously presented, flawlessly executed, and sets an exemplary benchmark for verifiable algorithmic number theory.
weaknesses: The reliance on external companion preprints for analytic pillars (e.g., elliptic curve existence and function-field theorems) means full end-to-end formalization remains an open frontier.
